newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks up slightly at lunch, buying of banks.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks up slightly at lunch, buying of banks.

text.p: Despite some profit-taking early on Thursday, Thai stocks were up slightly in thin trade by the lunch break as local support funds bought large capitalised banking stocks, brokers said.

"I think the market rebounded this morning after some local support funds bought banking stocks because they believed prices were cheap now. Foreigners were still on the sidelines because they're dissatisfied with new central bank's measures," said Somnuk Chanrasamee of Nava Finance.
The index, which declined to a 97-month low on Wednesday, rose 3.05 points to 524.45 on 1.4 billion baht turnover.
Brokers said the Bank of Thailand's measures on the baht, announced on Tuesday, would prevent foreign investors from being active in the market and this would have a psychological impact on locals.
They said investors would now invest for short-term only as they did not want to take risks.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list by lunch, gaining 1.50 baht to 94.50. Noble Development NOBL.BK, debuted today in the property sector, was at 8.80, down from its IPO price of 16 baht.
